nodes.goal: Every confirmed defect, misleading message and small gap reported against 0.3.1rc1 is fixed before the next release candidate.
nodes.title: 0.3.1 pre-final fixes from rc1 feedback

acceptance: do-next-available-task skips a leaf whose sheet contains the scaffold-planning or promote placeholder text and whose node has no acceptance, and says why
grind-session --plan lists such leaves as not ready with the reason; --allow-unauthored overrides
validate prints one block naming every such open leaf (capped like the acceptance warning) and validate --all prints them all
A leaf whose sheet was filled in, or whose node has acceptance, is picked up as before
nodes.goal: An agent is never handed a leaf whose sheet still carries the scaffold or promote placeholder text and whose node has no acceptance criteria.
nodes.title: Refuse to pick up leaves whose planning sheet is still a placeholder

acceptance: handoff status on a leaf with records under work/reviews/<ID>/ but no claim reports those records and their verdicts instead of calling them leftover
The hint names `--ref <branch>` and `do-next-available-task --local`, never the pushing pickup
docs/orchestration.md states that records are read from the working tree, are untracked by design, that policy comes from the integration branch, and that approvals persist as Reviewed-by trailers
nodes.goal: A repository that never pushes claims can see the state of its review records and is never told to run a pushing command.
nodes.title: handoff status reports review records without a claim

acceptance: docs/roadmap-authoring.md explains that every write renders chunks in one canonical key order, so the first edit of a hand-authored chunk rewrites all of it and later diffs stay confined
rebalance-chunks --normalize rewrites every chunk in canonical form without moving a node, and is a no-op on already-canonical chunks
A test covers normalize on a hand-ordered chunk and its idempotence
nodes.goal: A PM is not surprised when a first edit reorders every node of a hand-authored chunk, and can normalise a chunk on purpose.
nodes.title: Document the canonical chunk key order and offer a deliberate normalisation

acceptance: The specyrd-brainstorm skill and the managed AGENTS.md block say to run `brainstorm start` before reading the digest or roadmap

The round-1 prompt tells the agent to propose an answer per framing question from what the PM already said, mark answered ones 'assumed', and lists the canonical frame keys (including deadline and budget), with outcome, served, not-the-question and assumed-vs-known marked required
`--panel N` shard cells are derived from the recorded allocation when one exists, and shard prompts carry the recorded frame
Each pass writes its own prompt file (-r1-, -r2-, -recommend-, -evidence-) and nothing overwrites an earlier pass's prompt
Prompts omit the 'roadmap-context.md (missing)' line when the file is absent
`brainstorm start` warns when run on the integration branch and suggests chore/brainstorm-<slug>
Every command prints the next step in order (round -> recommend -> evidence/verify -> triage -> promote)
nodes.goal: A brainstorm run by an agent starts without anchoring on the roadmap, frames the question without a cold questionnaire, and keeps every pass's prompt for audit.
nodes.title: Brainstorm prompts: shards from the allocation, per-pass files, framing with proposed answers

acceptance: `recommend --check` exits non-zero and lists every idea without a cluster or a recommendation
`list --by cluster` prints critic lines only with --show-verdicts
`evidence` defaults to strong ideas and warns when more than 15 ideas are selected
`verify` records a matched quote as `matched` (and still reads `retrieved` from older sessions)
`promote` warns for each strong idea whose sources are unverified
nodes.goal: A converge pass that misses an idea, an evidence pass that is too wide, or a verdict resting on unverified evidence is reported before promote.
nodes.title: Converge and evidence passes that cannot silently skip work

acceptance: `accept`/`reject`/`park` check every idea id before changing anything and print nothing on failure
`brainstorm realize <IDEA> --node <ID>` records a node created outside promote as the idea's promoted node
`revise --append-why` adds to the verdict reasoning; `--why` help names the stored field
`list --summary` prints per-status and per-recommendation counts
`--reason` is required by park and reject and optional on accept, and the help says so for each
nodes.goal: The PM can finish triage without scripts and without a partial write.
nodes.title: Triage commands: realize, append-why, summary, consistent reasons, all-or-nothing accept

acceptance: promote validates once after all nodes are written, so warnings print once
Derived codenames are capped (first four words, collision-checked) and the idea's `--codename` on revise wins
The idea's hypothesis is copied to the node's goal when present; sibling order follows the accept order
After promoting, one list names the nodes still without acceptance or touch zones
nodes.goal: Promoted nodes have a goal, a sane codename and a stable order, and promote reports once what is still missing.
nodes.title: promote writes usable nodes once, with short codenames

acceptance: validate warns once when the running version differs from a pin declared in .specyrd/manifest.json or requirements*.txt
The AGENTS.md section warning says the section differs from what this version writes, not 'from another version'
`upgrade` copies shipped docs the load order names (docs/supply-chain-security.md) when missing, and validate warns on a load-order path that does not exist
`refresh-stubs --dry-run` prints a one-line migration summary (N command stubs become skills)
edit-node warns when a list field receives a value that looks like a JSON list
The parent-status warning fires only when a stored Complete disagrees with a non-Complete rollup or vice versa; an In Progress parent with a Not Started rollup is not told to downgrade
`specy-road version` is an alias of `--version`, and an unknown command exits non-zero
nodes.goal: An adopter can tell a deliberate upgrade from an accidental one and is not sent to files they do not have.
nodes.title: Upgrade and validate report drift and migrations plainly

acceptance: A roster channels.cli can name `{session_flag}` which expands to `--session-id <id>` on launch and `--resume <id>` on resume for claude-code, so one command serves both, and docs/orchestration-workers.md documents it and the harness settings-file route

orchestrate plan prints the ref the roster was read from, and when the local roadmap/orchestration.yaml is absent there or differs it says so instead of the may_process hint; validate warns the same way
worker sync reports a gap in event sequence numbers
session start --path accepts several values
nodes.goal: A custom worker command keeps its permissions across resumes, the plan says where its roster came from, and lost events are reported.
nodes.title: Worker and session CLI: resume permissions, roster provenance, event gaps
